audit.recode_to: Right-edge, weight-sensitive penultimate (catalog classification weight or 'weight-hedged'; edge=right; heavy = long vowel (CVV) in the FINAL syllable only; not in the strict set, dom pattern = penult penultimate stress): 'Stress normally occurs on the final syllable if it contains a long vowel, otherwise on the penultimate syllable. However, in trisyllabic words where the last syllable is initiated by /h/, stress is antepenultimate: /ˈhereho/ 'thing', /mʷaˈeraha/ 'chief'.' quote/cite/loc = Lynch, John & Rex Horoi 2002, 'Arosi', in Lynch, Ross & Crowley (eds.) The Oceanic Languages, p. 563 sec. 1.3 'Stress' (p. 580 of the scan we hold). Keep Capell 1971:7-8 as older-primary supporting source (his 4-syllable transcriptions,konoˈkono, hiniˈhini, na,tahiˈana, na,rumaˈnas(i), rongoiˈsuri all show penultimate main stress; his 'initial' trisyllables ˈmwaeraha and hereˈho-type forms are exactly L&H's /h/-antepenult sub-case; only ˈarosi is a residual exception). Add contra entries: StressTyp2 2015 'I' and WALS 14A 'Initial' (both from Capell 1971:7) are database errors arising from disyllables where initial = penult.

(2) Deciding source: the initial 'fixed-strict' code is inherited from StressTyp2 (2015), a secondary database whose sole source is Capell 1971:7, a 90-pp grammar sketch; WALS 14A codes the same from the same page.
